title: Differences of electric potential play a great part in cell division

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Differences of electric potential play a great part in cell division

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Differences of electric potential between cell constituents, and between parts of the egg, play a great part in cell division; the potential difference between animal and vegetative poles of a fertilised egg fluctuates or reverses at successive segmentations, and the electrical difference of chromatin is greatest at mitosis.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Among other investigations, all leading towards the same general conclusion, namely that differences of electric potential play a great part in the phenomenon of cell division

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Electrical potential in cell division”. Scope: dividing cells and fertilised eggs (e.g. Fundulus, toad, turtle)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-08: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is experimentally testable with modern voltage reporters and perturbations. Existing public data are unlikely to provide the species, spatial calibration, successive segmentations, and causal interventions needed for the full statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure membrane or intracellular electrical potential spatially through successive cleavages while simultaneously imaging division timing, chromatin, and polarity; perturb voltage independently and quantify effects on division. Support requires reproducible pole differences or reversals that causally alter segmentation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical 'potential' does not map uniquely to membrane voltage.

Public embryo datasets rarely combine calibrated voltage and full cleavage imaging.

Association would not establish the asserted major causal role.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The concrete electrical patterns Thompson cites are measurable, and classic recordings for fish and amphibian eggs can be compiled. They cover few species, and correlation with cleavage does not show that the potential difference does causal work. Clamping experiments that would settle the causal share are sparse, so only a proxy test is available.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Align membrane or pole-to-pole potential of fertilised eggs with the cleavage cycle, and ask whether the animal-vegetal difference reverses at successive divisions and whether chromatin's electrical contrast peaks at mitosis. A large causal contribution, shown by division failing when those differences are clamped, would support the claim; potential fluctuations that are dispensable for division would refute a 'great part' in the process.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Potential changes can be consequences of membrane events rather than drivers of the division plane.

'A great part' has no numerical threshold.

Voltage traces aligned to cleavage exist for a few eggs and are not in one archive.
